docs.title: M01 · AI Fluency: Framework & Foundations
docs.text: Open on Skilljar

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Introduces the AI Fluency Framework — a structured approach to effective, ethical, and safe human-AI collaboration. This is the conceptual foundation for the entire AI Fluency series.

docs.title: The 4D Competencies
docs.text: Competency Focus Delegation Deciding what to hand off to AI and when Description Communicating clearly to get the output you need Discernment Evaluating, verifying, and improving AI outputs Diligence Taking responsibility for AI-assisted work

docs.title: Sections
docs.text: # Section S01 Introduction to AI Fluency S02 The AI Fluency Framework S03 What is Generative AI? S04 Delegation S05 Description S06 Effective Prompting Techniques S07 Discernment S08 The Description–Discernment Loop S09 Diligence S10 Conclusion

docs.title: Deep Dives
docs.text:
• What is Generative AI?
  • Capabilities and limitations
  • Practical prompting techniques

docs.title: Learning Outcomes
docs.text:
• A framework for thinking about AI interactions
  • The ability to make informed decisions about when and how to engage with AI systems
  • Practical skills for more fluent human-AI collaboration
  • Confidence in evaluating and taking responsibility for AI output

docs.title: Key Takeaways
docs.text:
• This course focuses on human-AI collaboration, not just understanding AI as a technology.
  • AI Fluency means engaging with AI systems effectively, efficiently, ethically, and safely.
  • The AI Fluency Framework centers on the "4D" competencies of Delegation, Description, Discernment, and Diligence.
  • The goal is to develop lasting skills that remain relevant as AI technology evolves.
  • Effective AI collaboration requires both practical skills and a fundamental shift in how we think about working with AI.

docs.title: Putting Things into Practice
docs.text:
You will need access to a language model (5-10 minutes).

Throughout this course, you will practice what you are learning by working directly with a language model. While our examples feature Claude (Anthropic's AI assistant), you are welcome to work with any language model you prefer. The principles and skills we explore apply across different AI systems.

Getting started is simple and free:

  • Claude: Visit claude.ai to create a free account
  • No paid subscriptions are required to complete course activities
  • You can also use other AI chatbots if you prefer
  • New to Claude? No worries. We will provide clear guidance with each exercise to help you get started

docs.title: Reflection
docs.text:
Before moving on, take a moment to consider your own experiences with AI:

  • What challenges have you encountered when working with AI to achieve specific outcomes?
  • What possibilities for AI collaboration excite you most?
  • What do you hope to gain from this course?

docs.title: Why Do We Need AI Fluency?
docs.text:
AI Fluency involves developing practical skills, knowledge, insights, and values that help you interact with AI systems in ways that are effective, efficient, ethical, and safe.

We also introduce three ways people engage with AI:

  • Automation: The AI completes specific tasks based on your instructions
  • Augmentation: You and AI collaborate as creative thinking and task execution partners
  • Agency: You configure AI to work independently on your behalf, establishing its knowledge and behavior patterns rather than just giving it specific tasks

docs.title: What Is AI Fluency?
docs.text: AI Fluency means interacting with AI systems in ways that are Effective, Efficient, Ethical, and Safe.

docs.title: Three Ways to Interact with AI
docs.text:
• Automation: AI does the work for you, following explicit instructions
  • Augmentation: You and AI work collaboratively together
  • Agency: AI works independently on your behalf

docs.title: The 4D Framework
docs.text:
The four core competencies of AI Fluency are the "4Ds": Delegation, Description, Discernment, and Diligence.

  • Delegation: Thoughtfully deciding what work to do with AI vs. doing yourself
  • Description: Communicating clearly with AI systems
  • Discernment: Evaluating AI outputs and behavior with a critical eye
  • Diligence: Ensuring you interact with AI responsibly

We explore how these competencies work together across different ways of engaging with AI, and why developing these skills prepares you for whatever AI evolution brings next.

docs.title: Key Takeaways
docs.text:
• AI Fluency means engaging with AI in ways that are effective, efficient, ethical, and safe
  • There are three primary ways we engage with AI:
    • Automation: AI executes specific tasks based on your instructions
    • Augmentation: You and AI collaborate as creative thinking and task execution partners
    • Agency: You guide AI to work independently on your behalf, shaping its knowledge and behavior rather than specific actions
  • The AI Fluency Framework consists of four core competencies (the 4Ds):
    • Delegation: Deciding what work to do with AI vs. yourself
    • Description: Communicating effectively with AI systems
    • Discernment: Evaluating AI outputs critically
    • Diligence: Ensuring responsible AI collaboration
  • These competencies apply across all three ways of working with AI
  • Developing these competencies prepares you for evolving AI capabilities

docs.title: Exercise 1: Apply the 4Ds
docs.text:
Estimated time: 5 minutes

Pick one of these collaboration scenarios and consider how you might apply the 4D Framework.

docs.title: Communication Project
docs.text:
You are working with an AI assistant to draft a series of emails for a marketing campaign.

  • Delegation: What aspects of this project would you handle yourself vs. collaborate on with AI?
  • Description: How would you communicate your vision for the campaign's tone, purpose, and success criteria to the AI?
  • Discernment: What criteria would help you evaluate whether the AI-drafted emails meet your needs?
  • Diligence: What considerations around transparency and responsibility would be important?

docs.title: Research Project
docs.text:
You are using AI to help analyze a large dataset for a research paper.

  • Delegation: How would you divide the analytical work between yourself and the AI?
  • Description: What context would the AI need to understand about your research question to do its share of the tasks well?
  • Discernment: How would you verify the AI's analysis for accuracy?
  • Diligence: What ethical considerations might arise when publishing AI-assisted research?

docs.title: Creative Project
docs.text:
You are collaborating with AI to develop character concepts for a story.

  • Delegation: What creative elements would you want to explore through AI collaboration vs. develop independently?
  • Description: How might you guide the AI to generate characters that fit your story's world?
  • Discernment: How would you decide which AI-suggested elements to keep, modify, or discard?
  • Diligence: How would you acknowledge AI's contribution to your creative work?

docs.title: Exercise 2: Explore Something You Love
docs.text:
Estimated time: 5-10 minutes

Spend 5-10 minutes chatting with Claude about a topic you are passionate about and know well. We will use Claude across exercises for the rest of the course, but you can also do these exercises with another AI. It may also be worthwhile to try the exercises across this course with several AI assistants to get a feel for how they differ.

Instructions:

  • Choose a topic you know well and enjoy discussing, such as a hobby, professional interest, favorite book series, etc.
  • Have a natural conversation with Claude about this topic, like you would with someone who shares your interest.
  • Try to notice moments where:
    • Claude enhances your thinking
    • You need to clarify or correct Claude's understanding
    • Your expertise leads you to evaluate Claude's responses

docs.title: Exercise 3: Learn Something New
docs.text:
Estimated time: 5-10 minutes

Spend 5-10 minutes asking Claude to teach you about a topic you are unfamiliar with but interested in exploring. See how this experience differs from your conversation about something you love and know well.

Instructions:

  • Choose a topic you would like to learn more about
  • Engage Claude in a conversation to help you understand the basics of this topic. Do not worry about prompting the "wrong way" or the "right way". Just ask Claude to teach you
  • Try to notice moments where Claude:
    • Offers helpful explanations
    • Provides examples that make abstract ideas concrete
    • Responds naturally to your questions as they arise
    • Explains things where you would want to double-check its explanations

docs.title: Reflection
docs.text:
Before moving on, take a moment to consider:

  • Which of the 4Ds (Delegation, Description, Discernment, Diligence) do you feel most confident in already? Which might need more development?
  • Can you recall a recent AI interaction where the framework might have helped?
  • What specific skills from the 4D framework would most enhance your work or personal projects?

This knowledge will provide valuable context for the 4Ds and especially strengthen your Delegation competence.

docs.title: What Is Generative AI?
docs.text:
• Generative AI refers to artificial intelligence systems that can create new content rather than simply analyze existing data.
  • Example:
  • Traditional AI: Classifies emails as spam or not spam.
  • Generative AI: Creates a brand-new email.
  • This represents a shift from analyzing and categorizing information to generating new content.

docs.title: Large Language Models (LLMs)
docs.text:
• LLMs are a major type of generative AI.
  • Examples include Anthropic's Claude models.
  • They are called:
  • Language Models because they are trained to understand and generate human language.
  • Large because they contain billions of parameters.
  • Parameters are mathematical values that influence how the model processes information, somewhat similar to neural connections in the human brain.

docs.title: Three Key Developments That Enabled Modern Generative AI
1. Algorithmic and Architectural Breakthroughs
docs.text:
• Neural networks have existed for decades.
  • The introduction of the Transformer Architecture in 2017 was a major breakthrough.
  • Transformers are effective at:
  • Processing sequences of text.
  • Maintaining relationships between words across long passages.
  • Understanding context and meaning.

docs.title: 2. Explosion of Digital Data
docs.text:
• Large language models learn from vast collections of text, including:
  • Websites
  • Books
  • Articles
  • Code repositories
  • Other digital content
  • This diverse data helps models develop:
  • Broad knowledge
  • Language understanding
  • Conceptual relationships

docs.title: 3. Increased Computational Power
docs.text:
• Training modern AI models requires enormous computing resources.
  • Important technologies include:
  • GPUs (Graphics Processing Units)
  • TPUs (Tensor Processing Units)
  • Distributed computing clusters
  • These technologies make large-scale model training possible.

docs.title: Scaling Laws
docs.text:
• Researchers discovered that model performance improves predictably when:
  • Models become larger.
  • More data is used.
  • More computational power is available.

docs.title: Emergent Capabilities
docs.text:
As models scale, unexpected abilities emerge, including:

  • Step-by-step reasoning
  • Problem solving
  • Adapting to unfamiliar tasks
  • Learning from minimal instructions

These capabilities were not explicitly programmed into the models.

docs.title: Pre-Training Process
docs.text:
• Models analyze billions of text examples.
  • Their primary objective is to:
  • Predict the next word (or token) in a sequence.
  • Through repeated prediction and correction, models learn:
  • Grammar
  • Language patterns
  • Facts and knowledge
  • Relationships between concepts

docs.title: Outcome
docs.text:
• The model builds a complex statistical representation of:
  • Language
  • Knowledge
  • Human communication patterns

docs.title: Fine-Tuning
docs.text: After pre-training, models undergo fine-tuning.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
Fine-tuning teaches models to:

  • Follow instructions
  • Generate useful responses
  • Avoid harmful content
  • Improve overall performance

docs.title: Human Feedback
docs.text:
• Humans evaluate and rate model responses.
  • Feedback helps improve model behavior.

docs.title: Reinforcement Learning
docs.text:
• Rewards desirable outputs.
  • Penalizes undesirable outputs.
  • Encourages models to become:
  • Helpful
  • Honest
  • Harmless

docs.title: How Interaction Works
docs.text:
When a user interacts with an LLM:

  1. The user provides a prompt.
  2. The model reads the prompt.
  3. The model generates a response based on learned patterns.

docs.title: Important Note
docs.text:
• LLMs do not retrieve pre-written answers from a database.
  • They generate new responses dynamically based on probabilities learned during training.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
The context window is the amount of information a model can consider at one time.

It functions like the AI's working memory.

docs.title: What It Includes
docs.text:
• User prompts
  • Previous AI responses
  • Shared conversation information

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Models cannot access information outside the current context window.
  • Additional tools may be required, such as:
  • Web search
  • Retrieval systems
  • External databases

docs.title: Three Characteristics That Make Modern Generative AI Powerful
1. Learning from Vast Amounts of Information
docs.text:
• Training on enormous datasets enables models to learn:
  • Complex language patterns
  • World knowledge
  • Conceptual relationships

docs.title: 2. In-Context Learning
docs.text:
• Models can adapt to new tasks using:
  • Instructions
  • Examples
  • Prompt guidance
  • Additional training is often unnecessary.

docs.title: 3. Emergent Capabilities
docs.text:
• New abilities appear as models become larger.
  • These capabilities can exceed what researchers initially expected.

docs.title: Key Takeaways
docs.text:
• Generative AI creates new content rather than simply analyzing data.
  • LLMs rely on the Transformer architecture and billions of parameters.
  • Three major factors enabled modern AI:
  • Transformer-based breakthroughs
  • Massive amounts of training data
  • Increased computing power
  • Models learn through next-word prediction during pre-training.
  • Fine-tuning improves helpfulness, safety, and instruction

docs.title: What Generative AI Can and Cannot Do
docs.text: Understanding the strengths and limitations of generative AI helps us use it more effectively. Like learning how a new colleague works best, knowing where AI excels and where it struggles allows for better collaboration.

docs.title: What LLMs Do Well
docs.text: Modern Large Language Models (LLMs) are highly versatile and capable across a wide range of language tasks.

docs.title: Language Generation and Communication
docs.text:
LLMs can:

  • Draft emails that match a desired tone or style.
  • Summarize long documents into concise key points.
  • Translate text between languages.
  • Explain complex topics in simple terms.
  • Create content such as:
  • Articles
  • Reports
  • Poems
  • Brainstorming ideas
  • Marketing copy

docs.title: Adaptability Across Tasks
docs.text:
One of the most remarkable capabilities of LLMs is their ability to switch between tasks without additional training.

Examples include:

  • Writing creative content.
  • Planning events.
  • Explaining scientific concepts.
  • Analyzing business trends.
  • Assisting with coding tasks.

The same model can perform all of these tasks through natural conversation.

docs.title: Conversational Memory
docs.text:
LLMs can maintain context throughout a conversation.

For example:

  • A user mentions a project deadline early in the discussion.
  • Later references "the deadline."
  • The model can typically understand what is being referenced and continue the conversation accordingly.

docs.title: Tool Use and External Knowledge
docs.text:
Many modern AI systems can connect to external tools, enabling them to:

  • Search the web.
  • Analyze files and documents.
  • Access databases.
  • Use software applications.

These capabilities significantly expand what AI can help accomplish.

docs.title: What LLMs Cannot Do Well
docs.text: Despite their impressive abilities, LLMs have important limitations.

docs.title: 1. Knowledge Cutoff Limitations
docs.text: LLMs are trained on data available up to a specific point in time.

docs.title: Knowledge Cutoff
docs.text:
• Every model has a training cutoff date.
  • Information after that date is not part of the model's built-in knowledge.
  • Without external tools, the model cannot inherently know about newer events.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
A model trained through November 2024 would not automatically know about:

  • Events occurring after November 2024.
  • Newly published research.
  • Recently released products.
  • Current news.

To access current information, the model needs tools such as:

  • Web search
  • Databases
  • Retrieval systems

docs.title: 2. Hallucinations
docs.text: LLMs can sometimes generate information that sounds convincing but is incorrect.

docs.title: What Is a Hallucination?
docs.text:
A hallucination occurs when a model:

  • Produces inaccurate information.
  • Invents facts, sources, dates, or details.
  • States incorrect information confidently.

docs.title: Why Hallucinations Happen
docs.text:
Because LLMs:

  • Generate responses based on learned patterns.
  • Do not verify every statement against a factual database.
  • May combine information incorrectly.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
An AI might confidently provide:

  • An incorrect citation.
  • A nonexistent research paper.
  • An inaccurate historical fact.

This is similar to a person confidently telling a story while getting some details wrong.

docs.title: 3. Context Window Constraints
docs.text: LLMs have a limited amount of information they can consider at one time.

docs.title: Context Window
docs.text:
The context window includes:

  • User prompts
  • AI responses
  • Documents provided during the interaction

docs.title: Limitation
docs.text:
Once the context window is exceeded:

  • Older information may be dropped.
  • The model may forget earlier details.
  • Large documents may become difficult to process fully.

This is often handled on a first-in, first-out basis.

docs.title: 4. Non-Deterministic Behavior
docs.text: Unlike traditional software, LLMs do not always provide identical outputs.

docs.title: What This Means
docs.text:
If you ask the same question multiple times:

  • The response may vary slightly.
  • Different wording or examples may be produced.
  • The overall answer may remain similar but not identical.

docs.title: Why This Happens
docs.text:
LLMs generate text probabilistically.

They predict:

"What is the most likely next word or token?"

rather than retrieving a fixed response.

docs.title: Temperature
docs.text:
Developers can control response randomness through a setting called temperature.

  • Lower temperature:
  • More predictable

  • More consistent

  • Higher temperature:

  • More creative
  • More varied

docs.title: 5. Challenges with Complex Reasoning
docs.text:
Historically, LLMs have struggled with:

  • Multi-step mathematics
  • Formal logic problems
  • Complex reasoning chains

Examples include:

  • Mathematical proofs
  • Advanced calculations
  • Difficult logical puzzles

docs.title: Recent Improvements
docs.text:
Newer reasoning-focused models:

  • Break problems into steps.
  • Perform extended reasoning.
  • Produce more reliable results on complex tasks.

Significant progress continues in this area.

docs.title: 6. Limited Access to Data and Tools
docs.text: Even highly capable models can only work with the information and tools available to them.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Imagine a brilliant coworker who:

  • Understands the problem perfectly.
  • Cannot access the company's internal database.

Their ability to help is still limited.

Similarly, AI may be unable to complete a task if it lacks access to:

  • Internal systems
  • Proprietary databases
  • Specialized software
  • Required external tools

No amount of intelligence can compensate for missing information.

docs.title: Ongoing Improvements
docs.text:
Researchers are actively working to reduce current limitations.

Key approaches include:

docs.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
docs.text:
RAG allows models to:

  • Access external knowledge sources.
  • Retrieve current information.
  • Ground responses in real documents.

docs.title: Improved Tool Use
docs.text:
Modern systems are increasingly able to:

  • Search the web.
  • Analyze files.
  • Use APIs.
  • Interact with external applications.

docs.title: Enhanced Reasoning
docs.text:
Researchers continue improving:

  • Logical reasoning
  • Mathematical problem solving
  • Multi-step decision making

docs.title: The Human-AI Partnership
docs.text: The most effective use of AI combines the strengths of humans and machines.

docs.title: Human Strengths
docs.text:
Humans contribute:

  • Critical thinking
  • Judgment
  • Creativity
  • Domain expertise
  • Ethical decision-making
  • Contextual understanding

docs.title: AI Strengths
docs.text:
AI contributes:

  • Speed
  • Scalability
  • Pattern recognition
  • Information processing
  • Content generation
  • Consistency in repetitive tasks

Together, these strengths create more effective outcomes than either working alone.

docs.title: Why AI Fluency Matters
docs.text:
Understanding both AI capabilities and limitations helps users:

  • Choose appropriate use cases.
  • Verify important information.
  • Avoid overreliance on AI outputs.
  • Improve productivity.
  • Collaborate more effectively with AI systems.

As AI technology continues to evolve, ongoing learning and experimentation remain essential for staying current and discovering new possibilities.

docs.title: Key Takeaways
docs.text:
• LLMs excel at language generation, summarization, explanation, translation, and content creation.
  • They can adapt to many different tasks without additional training.
  • Modern models can maintain conversational context and use external tools.
  • LLMs are limited by:
  • Knowledge cutoffs
  • Hallucinations
  • Context window constraints
  • Non-deterministic outputs
  • Reasoning challenges
  • Limited tool and data access
  • Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), tool use, and advanced reasoning models are helping overcome many current limitations.
  • The most powerful applications combine human strengths such as judgment and creativity with AI strengths such as speed, scale, and pattern recognition.

docs.title: Delegation: Working Effectively with AI
docs.text:
Delegation is a core AI fluency competency focused on helping people work with AI in ways that are both effective and efficient. It involves deciding what work should be done, what work humans should handle, and what work can be delegated to AI.

Effective delegation is not simply about handing tasks to AI. It is about making thoughtful decisions that leverage the strengths of both humans and artificial intelligence.

docs.title: What Is Delegation?
docs.text:
At its core, delegation is the process of determining:

  • What work needs to be completed.
  • Which tasks should remain human-driven.
  • Which tasks are suitable for AI assistance.
  • How humans and AI can work together most effectively.

This often involves:

  • Breaking complex projects into smaller tasks.
  • Identifying opportunities for automation.
  • Using AI to augment human capabilities.
  • Deciding when human judgment is required.

docs.title: The Foundation of Effective Delegation
docs.text:
A surprising insight is that successful AI delegation starts with human expertise, not AI.

Before involving AI, it is important to clearly understand:

  • What you are trying to accomplish.
  • What problem you are solving.
  • What outcome you want to achieve.
  • What success looks like.

Without this understanding:

  • AI cannot compensate for unclear objectives.
  • It becomes difficult to evaluate AI outputs.
  • Human intervention may not occur when needed.

The best AI collaborators are:

Experts in their domain first and AI delegators second.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text: Problem Awareness is the ability to clearly define goals and understand the work required before using AI.

docs.title: Questions to Ask
docs.text:
Before involving AI, consider:

  • What am I trying to create, solve, or achieve?
  • What are the key project goals?
  • What does success look like?
  • What kind of thinking is required?

docs.title: Simple but Time-Consuming Tasks
docs.text:
Examples:

  • Data entry
  • Formatting documents
  • Summarizing information
  • Organizing content

These are often good candidates for AI assistance.

docs.title: Areas of Uncertainty
docs.text:
Situations where you need:

  • Brainstorming
  • Alternative perspectives
  • Idea generation

AI can act as a thought partner.

docs.title: Areas of Ignorance
docs.text:
Sometimes the challenge is lacking information rather than lacking ideas.

In these cases, you may need:

  • More research
  • Additional data
  • External information sources

docs.title: Areas Requiring Critical Judgment
docs.text:
Some tasks require:

  • Expertise
  • Context awareness
  • Ethical reasoning
  • Strategic decision-making

These often require strong human involvement.

docs.title: Why Problem Awareness Matters
docs.text:
Without a clear understanding of the problem:

  • AI may generate irrelevant outputs.
  • Results may not align with project goals.
  • It becomes difficult to identify mistakes.
  • Human oversight may be weakened.

Understanding the problem is the first step toward successful AI collaboration.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
Platform Awareness refers to understanding the strengths and limitations of various AI systems.

Not all AI platforms are the same.

Different systems may prioritize:

  • Speed
  • Accuracy
  • Creativity
  • Reasoning
  • Tool use
  • Specialized capabilities

docs.title: Understanding the AI Landscape
docs.text:
Effective delegation requires familiarity with available tools.

Questions to consider include:

  • Which model performs best for my task?
  • Which system is optimized for creativity?
  • Which system is optimized for accuracy?
  • Which system offers stronger reasoning abilities?
  • Which platform integrates with needed tools?

Because AI technology evolves rapidly, staying informed is important.

docs.title: Building Platform Awareness
docs.text: The best way to develop platform awareness is through experimentation.

docs.title: Practical Strategies
docs.text:
• Test multiple AI systems.
  • Compare outputs across platforms.
  • Explore strengths and weaknesses.
  • Use hands-on experience to guide future decisions.

Over time, this helps develop an understanding of:

  • When to use specific tools.
  • What each platform does best.
  • Where limitations may exist.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
Task Delegation is the strategic distribution of work between humans and AI.

Once you understand:

  1. The problem (Problem Awareness)
  2. The available AI tools (Platform Awareness)

You can determine how work should be divided.

docs.title: Deciding What AI Should Do
docs.text:
Ask yourself:

  • Which tasks are repetitive?
  • Which tasks can be automated?
  • Which tasks would benefit from AI assistance?
  • Which tasks require uniquely human judgment?

Different approaches may be appropriate for different parts of the same project.

docs.title: Automation
docs.text:
AI performs tasks independently.

Examples:

  • Drafting routine emails
  • Categorizing information
  • Generating summaries
  • Processing large amounts of data

Benefits:

  • Saves time
  • Reduces repetitive work
  • Improves efficiency

docs.title: Augmentation
docs.text:
Humans and AI work together.

Examples:

  • Brainstorming ideas
  • Reviewing drafts
  • Solving problems collaboratively
  • Refining content

Benefits:

  • Combines human expertise with AI speed.
  • Often produces better results than either working alone.

docs.title: Human-Only Work
docs.text:
Some tasks should remain primarily human-driven.

Examples:

  • Ethical decisions
  • Strategic leadership
  • High-stakes judgments
  • Sensitive interpersonal communication

These areas often require:

  • Context
  • Responsibility
  • Experience
  • Human values

docs.title: AI Agents Acting on Your Behalf
docs.text:
AI agents can perform routine actions independently.

Examples:

  • Scheduling meetings
  • Handling repetitive workflows
  • Monitoring systems
  • Managing routine interactions

This can increase efficiency while reducing manual effort.

docs.title: The Three Elements of Delegation
docs.text: Effective delegation consists of three connected competencies:

docs.title: 1. Problem Awareness
docs.text:
Understanding:

  • Goals
  • Desired outcomes
  • Required work
  • Success criteria

docs.title: 2. Platform Awareness
docs.text:
Understanding:

  • Available AI systems
  • Strengths and weaknesses
  • Capabilities and limitations
  • Appropriate use cases

docs.title: 3. Task Delegation
docs.text:
Strategically deciding:

  • What AI should do
  • What humans should do
  • What should be done collaboratively
  • What should not be delegated

docs.title: Human and AI Strengths
docs.text: Effective delegation recognizes that humans and AI bring different strengths.

docs.title: Human Strengths
docs.text:
Humans excel at:

  • Critical thinking
  • Judgment
  • Ethics
  • Creativity
  • Domain expertise
  • Contextual understanding

docs.title: AI Strengths
docs.text:
AI excels at:

  • Speed
  • Scale
  • Pattern recognition
  • Information processing
  • Content generation
  • Repetitive tasks

The goal is not to replace one with the other, but to combine their strengths.

docs.title: Key Takeaways
docs.text:
• Delegation is about deciding how work should be distributed between humans and AI.
  • Effective delegation begins with understanding the problem before involving AI.
  • Problem Awareness focuses on defining goals and understanding required work.
  • Platform Awareness focuses on understanding the strengths and limitations of available AI systems.
  • Task Delegation focuses on strategically dividing work between humans and AI.
  • Work can be handled through:
  • Automation
  • Augmentation
  • Human-only execution
  • AI agents acting on your behalf
  • The most effective AI collaboration comes from intentionally combining human judgment and expertise with AI speed and scalability.
  • Successful AI users are not those who delegate everything, but those who delegate thoughtfully.

docs.title: What You'll Learn
docs.text:
By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

  • Apply your understanding of Delegation to a practical multi-step project that you will continue working on throughout the course.

Estimated Time: 20 minutes

docs.title: Step 1: Choose Your Project
docs.text:
Select a medium-sized, multi-step project that you can work on during the remainder of the course.

Your project should be:

  • Substantial enough to involve multiple types of tasks.
  • Manageable enough to complete within approximately one hour of work.
  • Personally meaningful or interesting to you.

docs.title: Communication Projects
docs.text:
• Create a compelling presentation on a topic you know well.
  • Write a post or series of posts explaining a complex topic to a general audience.
  • Develop a proposal or pitch for an idea you would like to pursue.
  • Create a personal or professional biography with supporting materials.

docs.title: Research Projects
docs.text:
• Research and summarize the current state of an emerging technology or trend.
  • Analyze a dataset, identify patterns, and provide recommendations.
  • Compare multiple products, services, or approaches and make a recommendation.
  • Investigate a historical event and present findings in an engaging format.

docs.title: Creative Projects
docs.text:
• Outline a short story with fully developed characters and plot.
  • Design a simple website structure and content for key pages.
  • Develop a concept for a product, service, or experience.

docs.title: Learning Projects
docs.text:
• Create a structured learning plan for a new skill.
  • Build a curated collection of resources on a topic you're studying.
  • Develop a tutorial or step-by-step guide for a process you understand well.
  • Create study materials for a topic you want to master.

docs.title: Step 2: Project Vision and Goals
docs.text:
Start a conversation with Claude and share your project idea.

Work together until you have a clear vision of the final outcome.

Your discussion should help clarify:

  • What success looks like for the project.
  • Why the project is valuable or meaningful to you.
  • The desired outcomes and goals.
  • The overall vision for the finished result.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Develop a clear and well-defined understanding of:

  • Your objectives.
  • Your expected outcomes.
  • Your personal motivation for completing the project.

docs.title: Step 3: Task Breakdown and Delegation Analysis
docs.text: Use the Delegation framework to analyze your project with Claude.

docs.title: 1. Identify Major Tasks
docs.text:
Work together to determine the primary tasks required to complete the project.

Examples may include:

  • Research
  • Planning
  • Content creation
  • Analysis
  • Design
  • Review and refinement

docs.title: 2. Analyze Each Task
docs.text: For every task, discuss the following questions:

docs.title: Skills and Capabilities Needed
docs.text:
• What knowledge is required?
  • What skills are needed?
  • What AI capabilities could assist?

docs.title: Human Strengths
docs.text:
• Which aspects require human judgment?
  • Where is creativity especially important?
  • What tasks depend on experience or context?

docs.title: AI Strengths
docs.text:
• Which tasks could be automated?
  • Where can AI accelerate progress?
  • What repetitive or information-heavy work could AI handle?

docs.title: Human-AI Collaboration
docs.text:
• Where would collaboration produce the best results?
  • Which tasks benefit from both human expertise and AI assistance?

Important: Treat this as a genuine conversation. Challenge assumptions, ask follow-up questions, seek clarification, and stay open to new insights that emerge during the discussion.

docs.title: 3. Create a Delegation-Based Project Plan
docs.text:
Build a project plan that includes:

  • Major project tasks
  • Human responsibilities
  • AI responsibilities
  • Collaboration opportunities
  • Delegation decisions

docs.title: 4. Save Your Project Plan
docs.text:
Save your completed plan.

You will revisit this project later in the course to further develop the following AI Fluency competencies:

  • Description
  • Discernment
  • Diligence

docs.title: Reflection
docs.text:
Before continuing, take time to reflect on the planning process.

Consider the following questions:

docs.title: Insights
docs.text:
• What important insights emerged from your conversation with Claude?
  • Did any assumptions change during the discussion?

docs.title: Challenges
docs.text:
• What is likely to be the most difficult aspect of your delegation plan?
  • Where do you anticipate needing the most support?

docs.title: Growth Opportunities
docs.text:
• What information would help you delegate more effectively?
  • What additional skills could improve your ability to collaborate with AI?

docs.title: Key Deliverable
docs.text:
By the end of this exercise, you should have:

  • A clearly defined project.
  • A strong vision for success.
  • A task breakdown.
  • Delegation decisions for each task.
  • A reusable project plan for future course activities.

docs.title: What's Next
docs.text:
The next lesson focuses on the second core AI Fluency competency: Description.

You will learn how to communicate effectively with AI systems by:

  • Defining what you want clearly.
  • Guiding how AI approaches a task.
  • Specifying desired outputs.
  • Establishing how AI should interact with you throughout a project.

These skills will help you execute the project plan you created in this lesson.

docs.title: Feedback
docs.text:
As you progress through the course, consider sharing:

  • How you are applying AI Fluency concepts.
  • How you are using AI in your work, studies, or personal life.
  • Suggestions for improving the course experience.

docs.title: Description: Communicating Effectively with AI
docs.text:
The Description competency focuses on how we communicate with AI systems. It is a core component of AI fluency because the quality of AI outputs often depends on the quality of the instructions and context we provide.

Description is not just about writing prompts. It is about effectively guiding AI interactions by clearly communicating goals, context, expectations, methods, and desired behaviors.

docs.title: What Is Description?
docs.text:
Description is the ability to communicate effectively with AI in order to:

  • Explain tasks.
  • Ask questions.
  • Provide context.
  • Guide reasoning and problem-solving.
  • Correct misunderstandings.
  • Shape the overall interaction.

Think of Description as building a bridge between:

  • Your intentions
  • The AI's capabilities

The clearer the communication, the better the results.

docs.title: Why Description Matters
docs.text:
AI systems cannot read minds.

If instructions are vague, the AI must make assumptions, which can lead to:

  • Incomplete results
  • Incorrect outputs
  • Unwanted formats
  • Misaligned responses

Instead of assuming the AI knows what you want, clearly communicate:

  • The task
  • The context
  • The desired outcome
  • Any constraints or requirements

docs.title: Vague Request
docs.text: "Make dinner."

docs.title: Detailed Request
docs.text:
"Prepare a vegetarian pasta dinner for four people using ingredients commonly found at home. The meal should take less than 30 minutes and include a simple side dish."

The second description provides significantly more information, making it easier to achieve the desired result.

The same principle applies when working with AI.

docs.title: The Three Components of Description
docs.text:
The Description competency consists of three key elements:

  1. Product Description
  2. Process Description
  3. Performance Description

Together, they create a framework for effective AI communication.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
Product Description is the ability to clearly define what you want the AI to create or provide.

It focuses on the final output.

docs.title: Questions to Consider
docs.text:
When describing the desired product, ask:

  • What exactly do I want?
  • What is the goal?
  • What format should the response use?
  • Who is the audience?
  • What level of detail is needed?
  • What tone or style should be used?

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
Provide background information that helps the AI understand the situation.

Examples:

  • Business environment
  • Educational setting
  • Personal goals
  • Target audience

docs.title: Desired Outcome
docs.text:
Clearly explain what should be produced.

Examples:

  • Report
  • Email
  • Summary
  • Lesson plan
  • Presentation
  • Analysis

docs.title: Format Requirements
docs.text:
Specify:

  • Length
  • Structure
  • Layout
  • Output format

Examples:

  • Markdown
  • Bullet points
  • Executive summary
  • Table
  • Blog post

docs.title: Audience
docs.text:
Identify who will consume the output.

Examples:

  • Students
  • Managers
  • Customers
  • Technical professionals
  • General public

docs.title: Product Description Example
docs.text: Create a one-page summary of cloud security best practices for new IT administrators. Use simple language, bullet points, and include practical examples. The audience is early-career infrastructure professionals.

docs.title: Key Idea
docs.text:
Product Description answers:

"What do you want the AI to create?"

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
Process Description is the ability to guide how the AI approaches a task.

It focuses on the method rather than just the final outcome.

docs.title: Why Process Matters
docs.text:
Sometimes how a task is performed is as important as the final result.

Just as you might ask a colleague to follow a particular process, you can guide AI in a similar way.

docs.title: General Guidance
docs.text:
Provide broad instructions.

Example:

Focus on practical recommendations rather than theoretical discussion.

docs.title: Step-by-Step Instructions
docs.text:
Define a sequence of actions.

Example:

  1. Analyze the problem.
  2. Identify root causes.
  3. Provide solutions.
  4. Rank solutions by impact.

docs.title: Examples and Demonstrations
docs.text:
Show the AI what good output looks like.

Example:

Follow the style of this sample report.

docs.title: Questions to Consider
docs.text:
• What information should the AI use?
  • What order should tasks follow?
  • Should specific methods or frameworks be applied?
  • Are there constraints or requirements?
  • Should the AI focus on certain issues?

docs.title: Process Description Example
docs.text: First summarize the article, then identify key risks, and finally provide three actionable recommendations. Focus on security and compliance impacts.

docs.title: Key Idea
docs.text:
Process Description answers:

"How should the AI approach the task?"

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
Performance Description is the ability to define how the AI should behave during an interaction.

It focuses on interaction style and communication preferences.

docs.title: Why Performance Matters
docs.text:
AI is not a database or vending machine.

It is an interactive system whose behavior can be influenced by instructions.

Different situations require different types of AI behavior.

docs.title: Exploration vs. Precision
docs.text:
Do you want the AI to:

  • Explore many possibilities?
  • Help identify a single best answer?

docs.title: Challenge vs. Support
docs.text:
Do you want the AI to:

  • Challenge assumptions?
  • Act as a supportive assistant?

docs.title: Detailed vs. Concise
docs.text:
Do you want:

  • Comprehensive explanations?
  • Brief, direct answers?

docs.title: Transparency
docs.text:
Should the AI:

  • Explain its reasoning?
  • Simply provide results?

docs.title: Critical Thinking Partner
docs.text: Challenge my assumptions and identify weaknesses in my plan.

docs.title: Brainstorming Partner
docs.text: Generate as many creative possibilities as possible without evaluating them initially.

docs.title: Executive Assistant
docs.text: Keep responses concise, action-oriented, and professional.

docs.title: Teacher
docs.text: Explain concepts step by step and verify understanding before moving forward.

docs.title: Key Idea
docs.text:
Performance Description answers:

"How should the AI behave while helping me?"

docs.title: How the Three Elements Work Together
Product Description
docs.text:
Defines:

What should be created?

docs.title: Process Description
docs.text:
Defines:

How should it be created?

docs.title: Performance Description
docs.text:
Defines:

How should the AI interact with me?

When combined, these three elements create much more effective AI interactions.

docs.title: Product
docs.text: Create a project plan for migrating workloads to Microsoft Azure.

docs.title: Process
docs.text: Analyze requirements first, identify risks second, and then create a phased migration strategy.

docs.title: Performance
docs.text:
Act as a senior cloud architect. Be direct, practical, and challenge unrealistic assumptions.

This combination gives the AI clear direction across all aspects of the task.

docs.title: Key Takeaways
docs.text:
• Description is the AI Fluency competency focused on effective communication with AI systems.
  • AI outputs improve when goals, context, and expectations are clearly communicated.
  • AI cannot read minds and should not be expected to infer important details.
  • Product Description defines what the AI should create.
  • Process Description defines how the AI should approach the work.
  • Performance Description defines how the AI should behave during the interaction.
  • Combining all three elements transforms AI from a generic assistant into a more effective and personalized thinking partner.
  • Strong Description skills lead to better outcomes, fewer misunderstandings, and more productive human-AI collaboration.

docs.title: Effective Prompting: Applying the Description Competency
docs.text:
Prompting is one of the most practical skills when working with AI. At its core, prompting is simply the application of the Description competency: clearly communicating what you want, how you want it done, and how you want the AI to interact with you throughout the process.

Effective prompting is less about technical tricks and more about clear communication.

Think of it as giving instructions to a capable new colleague who is eager to help but needs enough context and guidance to perform the task successfully.

docs.title: What Is Prompt Engineering?
docs.text:
Prompt Engineering is the practice of designing effective instructions for AI systems.

It involves:

  • Asking clear questions.
  • Providing relevant context.
  • Defining expectations.
  • Guiding the AI toward the desired outcome.

Many prompt engineering principles are similar to effective human communication, including:

  • Clarity
  • Context
  • Examples
  • Explicit instructions

However, AI often requires greater specificity because it cannot naturally infer information the way humans can.

docs.title: Why Effective Prompting Matters
docs.text:
The quality of AI outputs often depends on the quality of your instructions.

Good prompts help AI understand:

  • What you want.
  • Why you want it.
  • How the result should look.
  • How it should approach the task.

Prompting is an iterative process that improves with experimentation and practice.

docs.title: Six Foundational Prompting Techniques
docs.text:
The video highlights six key techniques that significantly improve AI interactions:

  1. Give AI context.
  2. Show examples.
  3. Specify output constraints.
  4. Break tasks into steps.
  5. Ask AI to think first.
  6. Define role, style, or tone.

docs.title: Why It Matters
docs.text:
Context helps AI tailor responses to your specific needs, background, and goals.

Without context, the AI is forced to make assumptions.

docs.title: Basic Prompt
docs.text: Tell me about climate change.

docs.title: Improved Prompt
docs.text:
Explain three major impacts of climate change on agriculture in tropical regions with examples from the past decade.

This version provides:

  • A specific topic
  • Geographic scope
  • Timeframe
  • Desired focus

docs.title: Adding Personal Context
docs.text: The prompt becomes even stronger when additional background is included.

docs.title: Enhanced Example
docs.text:
Explain three major impacts of climate change on agriculture in tropical regions with examples from the past decade. I am preparing for a job interview at an agricultural research lab in Indonesia. I have a degree in ecology but limited knowledge of climate change. Provide a summary that helps me discuss the topic confidently during the interview.

Now the AI understands:

  • The user's goal
  • Existing knowledge level
  • Intended use of the information
  • Desired depth of explanation

docs.title: Key Idea
docs.text:
Provide context about:

  • Who you are
  • Why you're asking
  • How you'll use the response
  • Your existing knowledge level

docs.title: Why It Matters
docs.text:
Sometimes examples communicate expectations better than explanations.

This technique is often called:

  • Few-shot prompting
  • Example-based prompting

docs.title: Task
docs.text:
Convert technical language into plain English.

Instead of only describing the style, provide examples.

docs.title: Example Inputs
docs.text:
Original:

The quantum algorithm exhibits quadratic speedup.

Plain:

The new method solves problems roughly twice as fast as previous methods.

Original:

The interface leverages intuitive design paradigms.

Plain:

The design is easy to understand and use.

docs.title: Benefits
docs.text:
Examples help the AI understand:

  • Writing style
  • Formatting expectations
  • Tone
  • Patterns to follow

The more representative the examples are, the better the AI can match your expectations.

docs.title: Key Idea
docs.text:
Whenever possible:

Show the AI what good output looks like.

docs.title: Why It Matters
docs.text:
Clearly defining requirements helps ensure the output matches your expectations.

AI performs better when specific constraints are provided.

docs.title: Format
docs.text:
Examples:

  • Markdown
  • Table
  • Executive summary
  • Bullet points
  • Presentation outline

docs.title: Length
docs.text:
Examples:

  • One paragraph
  • 300 words
  • One-page summary

docs.title: Design Requirements
docs.text:
Examples:

  • Color palette
  • Layout structure
  • Page sections
  • User interface requirements

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Create a clean modern single-page art portfolio website with the following sections:

  • Hero
  • About Me
  • Skills
  • Portfolio Projects
  • Experience
  • Contact

Include a responsive navigation bar with a mobile hamburger menu, a sunset color palette, and a dark/light mode toggle.

docs.title: Key Idea
docs.text: The more clearly you define success, the easier it is for AI to produce useful output.

docs.title: Why It Matters
docs.text:
Large or complicated requests often benefit from structured instructions.

Breaking tasks into stages gives AI a clear process to follow.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Instead of:

Analyze this quarterly sales data.

Use:

Analyze this quarterly sales data by:

  1. Identifying the top-performing products.
  2. Comparing performance against the previous quarter.
  3. Highlighting unusual trends.
  4. Suggesting possible causes.
  5. Recommending actions.

docs.title: Benefits
docs.text:
Breaking a task into steps:

  • Improves organization.
  • Reduces ambiguity.
  • Produces more comprehensive responses.
  • Increases consistency.

docs.title: Key Idea
docs.text:
For complex tasks:

Explain both the destination and the route.

docs.title: Why It Matters
docs.text: For difficult questions, encouraging AI to reason through a problem before responding can improve answer quality.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: Before answering, think carefully through the problem. Consider relevant factors, constraints, and possible approaches before recommending the best solution.

docs.title: Benefits
docs.text:
This approach can:

  • Improve reasoning quality.
  • Produce more thoughtful responses.
  • Reveal assumptions.
  • Generate stronger recommendations.

docs.title: Important Principle
docs.text:
Reasoning should happen:

✅ Before the task is completed

Not:

❌ After the answer has already been generated

Giving AI space to think first often leads to better outcomes.

docs.title: Why It Matters
docs.text:
AI can adapt its communication style based on the role you assign.

Different situations benefit from different perspectives.

docs.title: Teacher Example
docs.text: Explain how rainbows form as an experienced science teacher speaking to a curious 10-year-old.

docs.title: Expert Example
docs.text: Act as a UX design expert and review this wireframe. Suggest three improvements focused on navigation and accessibility.

docs.title: Benefits
docs.text:
Role definitions help shape:

  • Expertise level
  • Perspective
  • Communication style
  • Depth of explanation

docs.title: Key Idea
docs.text:
Ask yourself:

Who do I want the AI to act as?

docs.title: The Secret Weapon: Ask AI to Improve Your Prompt
docs.text: When unsure how to phrase a request, ask the AI for help.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: I'm trying to achieve the following goal, but I'm not sure how to write an effective prompt. Can you help me craft a better prompt?

docs.title: Benefits
docs.text:
The AI can help:

  • Clarify requirements.
  • Improve structure.
  • Add missing context.
  • Suggest better wording.

docs.title: Prompting Is Iterative
docs.text:
Your first prompt will not always produce the best result.

That is normal.

Improvement comes through experimentation and refinement.

docs.title: Add More Context
docs.text:
Provide:

  • Goals
  • Background information
  • Intended audience

docs.title: Add Examples
docs.text: Show desired output styles.

docs.title: Break Tasks into Steps
docs.text: Guide the AI's process more explicitly.

docs.title: Request Variations
docs.text:
Example:

Give me three different versions.

docs.title: Change Output Formats
docs.text:
Example:

Present this as a checklist instead of paragraphs.

docs.title: Check Confidence
docs.text:
For factual questions ask:

How confident are you in this answer?

docs.title: Start Fresh
docs.text:
If a conversation becomes confusing or off-track:

  • Open a new chat.
  • Rephrase the request.
  • Try a different approach.

docs.title: Assuming AI Can Read Your Mind
docs.text:
Never assume important information is obvious.

Provide explicit details.

docs.title: Overloading One Prompt
docs.text: Avoid combining multiple unrelated tasks into a single request.

docs.title: Being Too Vague
docs.text:
Clearly define:

  • Goals
  • Requirements
  • Success criteria

docs.title: Not Providing Feedback
docs.text:
If the first response is imperfect:

  • Clarify expectations.
  • Refine instructions.
  • Continue the conversation.

docs.title: Best Practices for Effective Prompting
docs.text:
Successful prompts often include:

  • A clear task overview.
  • Relevant context.
  • Output specifications.
  • Examples when appropriate.
  • Explicit constraints.
  • Desired style or tone.

docs.title: Key Takeaways
docs.text:
• Prompting is the practical application of the Description competency.
  • Effective prompting combines human communication skills with AI-specific techniques.
  • The six core prompting techniques are:
  • Give context.
  • Show examples.
  • Specify constraints.
  • Break tasks into steps.
  • Ask AI to think first.
  • Define role, style, or tone.
  • AI performs best when instructions are clear, specific, and detailed.
  • Prompting is an iterative skill that improves through experimentation and practice.
  • One of the most effective prompting techniques is simply asking AI to help improve your prompt.
  • As AI systems evolve, specific techniques may change, but the principles of clear communication will remain valuable.

docs.title: Discernment: Evaluating AI Outputs, Processes, and Behaviors
docs.text:
The Discernment competency focuses on evaluating AI outputs, processes, and interactions. It serves as the quality control system for effective AI collaboration.

While Description is about communicating what you want, Discernment is about determining whether the AI's response actually meets your needs.

Discernment helps users:

  • Evaluate the quality of AI-generated work.
  • Identify strengths and weaknesses.
  • Detect errors and inaccuracies.
  • Improve future AI interactions.
  • Maintain human oversight and judgment.

docs.title: What Is Discernment?
docs.text:
Discernment is the ability to critically evaluate:

  • What the AI produces.
  • How the AI produces it.
  • How the AI behaves during interactions.

It allows users to determine:

  • Whether outputs are useful.
  • Whether outputs are reliable.
  • Whether additional refinement is required.
  • Whether a different approach is needed.

docs.title: Why Discernment Matters
docs.text:
Even advanced AI systems can:

  • Make factual mistakes.
  • Demonstrate faulty reasoning.
  • Misinterpret instructions.
  • Produce low-quality outputs.
  • Behave in unexpected ways.

Strong discernment helps prevent these issues from negatively affecting outcomes.

Effective AI use requires:

  • Domain expertise
  • Critical thinking
  • Understanding AI limitations

Human judgment remains an essential safeguard.

docs.title: The Three Components of Discernment
docs.text:
The Discernment competency consists of:

  1. Product Discernment
  2. Process Discernment
  3. Performance Discernment

Together they help users evaluate every aspect of AI collaboration.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
Product Discernment is the ability to evaluate the quality, accuracy, and value of AI-generated outputs.

It focuses on the final result.

docs.title: Questions to Ask
docs.text:
When reviewing AI-generated content, consider:

  • Is the information factually accurate?
  • Does it meet my requirements?
  • Is it relevant to the task?
  • Is it well-organized and coherent?
  • Is it appropriate for the intended audience?
  • Does it solve the problem I intended to address?
  • Does it add value?

docs.title: Accuracy
docs.text:
• Are facts correct?
  • Are sources reliable?
  • Are claims reasonable?

docs.title: Relevance
docs.text:
• Does the output address the actual request?
  • Does it remain focused on the objective?

docs.title: Quality
docs.text:
• Is the content clear and understandable?
  • Is the structure effective?
  • Is the writing professional and polished?

docs.title: Usefulness
docs.text:
• Can the output be used directly?
  • Does it require significant revisions?

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
If an AI generates a business proposal:

Product Discernment involves checking:

  • Whether recommendations are realistic.
  • Whether facts are accurate.
  • Whether the proposal aligns with business goals.
  • Whether it meets stakeholder expectations.

docs.title: Key Idea
docs.text:
Product Discernment answers:

"Is the output good?"

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
Process Discernment is the ability to evaluate how the AI arrived at its conclusions or outputs.

It focuses on the quality of the AI's reasoning and workflow.

docs.title: Why Process Matters
docs.text:
A correct answer obtained through flawed reasoning can still create problems.

For complex projects, evaluating the process becomes just as important as evaluating the final result.

docs.title: Logical Errors
docs.text:
The AI may:

  • Make unsupported assumptions.
  • Use flawed reasoning.
  • Reach conclusions that do not logically follow.

docs.title: Attention Lapses
docs.text:
The AI may:

  • Ignore important instructions.
  • Forget key details.
  • Focus on the wrong aspects of a task.

docs.title: Reintroducing Rejected Ideas
docs.text:
During iterative work, AI may:

  • Reinsert suggestions previously rejected.
  • Revive discarded concepts.
  • Lose track of agreed decisions.

docs.title: Circular Reasoning
docs.text:
The AI may:

  • Repeatedly reinforce the same conclusion.
  • Fail to explore alternatives.
  • Become trapped in repetitive reasoning patterns.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Suppose the AI proposes five outline options.

After selecting one, several discussion rounds occur.

If rejected ideas begin reappearing in later drafts:

  • The final output may still look acceptable.
  • However, the process indicates a problem.

This is something Process Discernment helps identify.

docs.title: Questions to Ask
docs.text:
• Is the reasoning sound?
  • Is the workflow logical?
  • Is the AI following agreed directions?
  • Is it considering alternatives appropriately?
  • Is it remaining aligned with project goals?

docs.title: Key Idea
docs.text:
Process Discernment answers:

"Is the AI working through the task effectively?"

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
Performance Discernment is the ability to evaluate the quality of the human-AI interaction itself.

It focuses on how the AI communicates and collaborates.

docs.title: Process
docs.text:
Evaluates:

The work the AI is doing.

docs.title: Performance
docs.text:
Evaluates:

How the AI interacts with you while doing the work.

docs.title: Questions to Ask
docs.text:
• Is the communication style helpful?
  • Is the interaction efficient?
  • Does the AI respond appropriately to feedback?
  • Is the level of detail appropriate?
  • Is the AI making collaboration easier or harder?

docs.title: Excessive Questioning
docs.text:
The AI may:

  • Ask too many follow-up questions.
  • Slow down progress unnecessarily.

docs.title: Excessive Brevity
docs.text:
The AI may:

  • Omit important details.
  • Provide insufficient explanations.

docs.title: Poor Adaptation
docs.text:
The AI may:

  • Ignore user preferences.
  • Fail to learn from corrections.
  • Continue repeating undesirable behaviors.

docs.title: Indicators of Strong Performance
docs.text:
A well-performing AI:

  • Communicates clearly.
  • Incorporates feedback effectively.
  • Matches the desired level of detail.
  • Adapts to user preferences.
  • Supports productive collaboration.

docs.title: Key Idea
docs.text:
Performance Discernment answers:

"Is the AI interacting with me effectively?"

docs.title: Discernment Leads to Feedback
docs.text:
Evaluation alone is not enough.

Once problems are identified, users should provide clear feedback.

docs.title: Identifying the Problem
docs.text:
Explain:

  • What is wrong.
  • What should be changed.

docs.title: Explaining Why
docs.text:
Help the AI understand:

  • Why the issue matters.
  • Why the current output is insufficient.

docs.title: Suggesting Improvements
docs.text:
Provide specific recommendations.

Examples:

  • Add more detail.
  • Use a different structure.
  • Focus on another audience.
  • Remove unnecessary content.

docs.title: Updating Instructions
docs.text:
Sometimes the original prompt needs improvement.

Examples:

  • Add context.
  • Clarify requirements.
  • Include examples.
  • Refine constraints.

docs.title: The Relationship Between Description and Discernment
docs.text: Description and Discernment work together in a continuous improvement cycle.

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Focuses on:

Communicating what you want.

docs.title: Discernment
docs.text:
Focuses on:

Evaluating whether you received it.

docs.title: Continuous Improvement Loop
docs.text:
1. Describe the task.
  2. Review the AI output.
  3. Evaluate product, process, and performance.
  4. Provide feedback.
  5. Improve the instructions.
  6. Repeat as needed.

This cycle steadily improves output quality.

docs.title: When Description May Not Be Enough
docs.text:
Sometimes poor results are not caused by poor instructions.

Other possibilities include:

  • Using the wrong AI tool.
  • Choosing the wrong model.
  • Delegating inappropriate tasks.
  • Using AI where human expertise is required.

In such situations, improving prompts alone may not solve the problem.

You may need to revisit:

  • Delegation decisions.
  • Tool selection.
  • Project strategy.

docs.title: How Discernment Supports AI Fluency
docs.text:
Strong discernment enables users to:

  • Detect AI errors.
  • Identify hallucinations.
  • Verify quality.
  • Refine workflows.
  • Improve collaboration.
  • Maintain human oversight.

It helps ensure that AI remains a tool guided by human judgment rather than an authority that is blindly trusted.

docs.title: Key Takeaways
docs.text:
• Discernment is the AI Fluency competency focused on evaluating AI outputs, processes, and behaviors.
  • Effective discernment requires both domain knowledge and an understanding of AI limitations.
  • Product Discernment evaluates the quality and value of AI-generated outputs.
  • Process Discernment evaluates how the AI approaches and reasons through a task.
  • Performance Discernment evaluates the quality of the human-AI interaction.
  • Strong discernment helps identify errors, weaknesses, and opportunities for improvement.
  • Feedback is a critical part of discernment and often leads to better descriptions and instructions.
  • Description and Discernment work together in a continuous cycle of communication, evaluation, and refinement.
  • Human judgment remains essential for effective and responsible AI collaboration.

docs.title: Project Execution with Description–Discernment Loops
docs.text: Estimated Time: 30–60 Minutes

docs.title: Learning Objectives
docs.text:
By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

  • Apply Description and Discernment skills to a real-world project.
  • Engage in productive Description–Discernment feedback loops.
  • Create results through human-AI collaboration that exceed what either humans or AI could achieve independently.

docs.title: Exercise: Project Execution with Description–Discernment Loops
docs.text: This exercise focuses on applying everything learned so far by executing the project you planned earlier using both Description and Discernment competencies.

docs.title: Step 1: Review Your Project Plan
docs.text:
Before beginning execution:

  • Retrieve the project plan created in Lesson 5.
  • Review your delegation decisions:
  • Which tasks require human expertise?
  • Which tasks can leverage AI capabilities?
  • Which tasks benefit from collaboration?
  • Refine the project plan if your understanding has evolved since it was originally created.

docs.title: Step 2: Prepare Your Description Strategy
docs.text:
Start a conversation with Claude and introduce your project.

Before execution, establish expectations using the three Description components.

docs.title: Product Description
docs.text:
Define:

  • The outputs you need from Claude.
  • Desired formats.
  • Writing style and tone.
  • Length requirements.
  • Expected level of detail.

Questions to consider:

  • What should Claude create?
  • What should the final result look like?
  • Who is the intended audience?

docs.title: Process Description
docs.text:
Define:

  • How Claude should approach the work.
  • Specific methodologies to use.
  • Frameworks to follow.
  • Preferred workflows or reasoning approaches.

Questions to consider:

  • Should Claude follow a particular process?
  • Are there required steps?
  • Are there preferred methods for analysis or creation?

docs.title: Performance Description
docs.text:
Define how Claude should interact with you.

Examples:

  • Concise or detailed responses
  • Supportive or critical feedback
  • Creative or analytical focus
  • Collaborative brainstorming or direct execution

Questions to consider:

  • What type of thinking partner do you need?
  • Should Claude challenge assumptions?
  • Should Claude prioritize efficiency or exploration?

docs.title: Discuss Expectations
docs.text:
Work with Claude to establish:

  • Shared goals
  • Working style
  • Communication preferences
  • Success criteria

This creates a strong foundation for collaboration.

docs.title: Step 3: Execute the Project Using Description–Discernment Loops
docs.text:
For each project task, follow a continuous loop of:

Describe → Discern → Refine → Integrate

docs.title: 1. Describe
docs.text: Use Description skills to clearly communicate what you need.

docs.title: Product Description
docs.text:
Be specific about:

  • Deliverables
  • Desired outcomes
  • Format
  • Quality expectations

docs.title: Process Description
docs.text:
Guide Claude's approach by specifying:

  • Methods
  • Steps
  • Frameworks
  • Reasoning process

docs.title: Performance Description
docs.text:
Define how Claude should engage with you.

Examples:

  • Provide detailed explanations
  • Challenge weak assumptions
  • Offer concise recommendations
  • Collaborate as a brainstorming partner

docs.title: 2. Discern
docs.text: Evaluate the quality of both the output and the interaction.

docs.title: Product Discernment
docs.text:
Evaluate:

  • Accuracy
  • Completeness
  • Relevance
  • Quality
  • Usefulness

Questions:

  • Does this meet my requirements?
  • Is it correct?
  • Does it solve the problem?

docs.title: Process Discernment
docs.text:
Evaluate:

  • The reasoning process
  • Task execution quality
  • Adherence to instructions

Questions:

  • Did Claude follow the intended process?
  • Were important factors considered?
  • Was the approach effective?

docs.title: Performance Discernment
docs.text:
Evaluate:

  • Communication quality
  • Collaboration experience
  • Adaptability

Questions:

  • Is Claude interacting in a useful way?
  • Is the level of detail appropriate?
  • Is the interaction efficient?

docs.title: 3. Refine
docs.text: Use discernment insights to improve future outputs.

docs.title: Provide Feedback
docs.text:
Clearly explain:

  • What worked well
  • What did not work
  • What should change

docs.title: Clarify Requirements
docs.text:
Update your Description if necessary.

Examples:

  • Add missing context
  • Refine objectives
  • Specify stronger constraints

docs.title: Request Iterations
docs.text:
Continue working with Claude until the output meets expectations.

Refinement is an expected and valuable part of the process.

docs.title: 4. Integrate Human Expertise
docs.text:
AI should support, not replace, human judgment.

Apply your own:

  • Experience
  • Creativity
  • Professional knowledge
  • Critical thinking

Remember to:

  • Add your unique perspective.
  • Make final decisions.
  • Select what to keep or reject.
  • Accept responsibility for the final outcome.

docs.title: Continue the Loop
docs.text:
Repeat the following cycle throughout your project:

Describe
    ↓
Discern
    ↓
Refine
    ↓
Integrate
    ↓
Repeat

Continue until your project is complete.

docs.title: Reflection
docs.text: After completing your project, consider the following questions.

docs.title: Description Patterns
docs.text:
• Which descriptions produced the best results?
  • What types of instructions were most effective?
  • What level of detail worked best?

docs.title: Effort Distribution
docs.text:
• Which required more effort:
  • Description?
  • Discernment?
  • Why do you think that was the case?

docs.title: Plan vs. Reality
docs.text:
• How closely did execution match your original project plan?
  • What adjustments were necessary?
  • Which delegation decisions proved most effective?

docs.title: Key Learning Outcome
docs.text:
Successful human-AI collaboration is not a one-time interaction.

High-quality results emerge through repeated cycles of:

  • Clear communication
  • Critical evaluation
  • Feedback
  • Iteration

The Description–Discernment loop enables continuous improvement throughout a project.

docs.title: What's Next
docs.text: The next lesson introduces the final AI Fluency competency:

docs.title: Diligence
docs.text:
While:

  • Delegation focuses on effective task distribution.
  • Description focuses on communication.
  • Discernment focuses on evaluation.

Diligence focuses on:

  • Ethics
  • Safety
  • Transparency
  • Accountability
  • Responsible AI use

You will learn how to ensure your AI collaborations are trustworthy, responsible, and aligned with ethical best practices.

docs.title: Feedback
docs.text:
As you continue through the course, consider sharing:

  • How you are applying AI Fluency concepts.
  • How AI is affecting your work, studies, or daily life.
  • Suggestions for improving the course.

Feedback Form: https://forms.gle/zURqLbVgdDqGhHZk9
